site.name: runeforge-docs
site.summary: runeforge-docs Fictional state-management JavaScript library "Runeforge" official documentation site (Redux / Zustand-style ergonomics). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Sticky topbar with brand+version pill, doc tabs, ⌘K search trigger, version selector, theme toggle, GitHub stars; **three-column layout**: left categorized TOC tree (5 sections, 26 items), center page with hero / install code-tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) / "Hello, store" code-tabs (5 framework adapters: Vanilla / React / Solid / Svelte 5 / Vue 3) with copy button / 3-tile "three things to remember" / 6-row why-table comparing to Redux / Zustand / Jotai / next-steps list / prev/next pager; right-side on-this-page TOC. - `guide-quickstart.html` — 5-minute tutorial. Step-by-step build of a counter store, todo list with derived store, async fetcher with `asyncSlice()`, and devtools install. Lots of code blocks and an info / success callout. - `guide-stores.html` — Stores reference. Store API table; reading + subscribing; immutability warning callout; composing with `derive()`; slicing with `store.select()`; SSR (`toJSON` / `fromJSON`); testing pattern. - `guide-actions.html` — Actions & selectors. Action rules; selector c

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Runeforge documentation site, validating navigation, interactive controls, code components, and responsive behavior across all known pages.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed through four phases: validating global controls and the landing page, testing the core documentation flows, interacting with the examples and API reference, and finally verifying responsive mobile behavior and accessibility. The run will focus on interactive elements like the search dialog, version selector, theme toggle, and code tab/copy components, while paying special attention to the small tap targets and missing input labels flagged in the prescan.
assumptions: The site is a static documentation site with no backend; version switching and search will alter the DOM or UI state but won't fetch new pages.
The ⌘K search trigger opens a modal dialog as indicated by the dialog count in the DOM.
Code tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun and framework adapters) and copy buttons are fully functional interactive JavaScript components.
Links pointing to '#' (e.g., Blog, Community, Subscriptions) are placeholder anchors and will not navigate to new content.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets across the topbar (Docs, API, Examples, Blog, Community, Search, Theme toggle, GitHub stars) and left TOC, which will severely impact mobile UX.
Missing input label on the version selector dropdown and potentially the search input, affecting screen reader accessibility.
Code tab switching and copy-to-clipboard functionality, which are critical for developer experience and often fail on static sites without proper JS focus/state management.
Examples page filter input and category buttons, ensuring they correctly filter the 12 examples without layout shift.

Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Getting started › Quickstart Quickstart · 5 minutes From zero to a working app. In the next five minutes you'll install Runeforge, build a counter, build a todo list, and wire up an async fetcher. By the end you'll have used 90% of the API. Prerequisites: Node 20+ (or Bun). The examples use React but everything maps 1:1 to Solid, Svelte, Vue, and vanilla JS. Step 1 · Install Create a fresh app with whatever template you like. Then install Runeforge and the React adapter. # inside your app directory npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Step 2 · A counter store The smallest useful store has one piece of state and one action. Both are inferred from the object you pass to forge(). // stores/counter.ts import { forge } from "runeforge"; export const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { increment: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), decrement: (s) => ({ count: s.count - 1 }), reset: () => ({ count: 0 }), }, }); Use it in a component with useStore: // Counter.tsx import { useStore } from "@runeforge/react"; import { counter } from "./stores/counter"; export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return (

{count}

); } Notice three things: No provider. The store is just an import — it's already global. The component subscribes to a selector (s.count), not the whole store. If another part of state changed, this component would not re-render. Actions are called like ordinary methods. There's no dispatch(). Step 3 · A todo list (and a derived store) For richer state, use a slice for todos and another for the filter. Then derive a third store that combines them. // stores/todos.ts import { forge, derive } from "runeforge"; export const todos = forge({ state: { items: [] as { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }[] }, actions: { add: (s, text: string) => ({ items: [...s.items, { id: Date.now(), text, done: false }] }), toggle: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => t.id !== id) }), clear: (s) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => !t.done) }), }, }); export const filter = forge({ state: { mode: "all" as "all" | "active" | "done" }, actions: { setMode: (s, mode) => ({ mode }), }, }); // derive() runs only when its inputs change. export const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => { if (f.mode === "all") return t.items; if (f.mode === "active") return t.items.filter(x => !x.done); return t.items.filter(x => x.done); }); In the component, you subscribe to the derived store the same way you subscribe to a regular one: const visible = useStore(visibleTodos); return visible.map(t => ); Step 4 · Async (the easy way) Async work belongs in effects. Effects can read and write any store, await whatever they want, and report status into a status field. Runeforge ships an asyncSlice() helper that gives you a typed status object for free. import { forge, asyncSlice } from "runeforge"; export const users = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice() }, actions: { async load(s) { if (s.status === "loading") return s; try { const r = await fetch("/api/users"); const data = await r.json(); return { status: "ready", data, error: null }; } catch (e) { return { status: "error", data: null, error: e.message }; } }, }, }); Inside the component: const { status, data, err

Step 1 · Install Create a fresh app with whatever template you like. Then install Runeforge and the React adapter. # inside your app directory npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Step 2 · A counter store The smallest useful store has one piece of state and one action. Both are inferred from the object you pass to forge(). // stores/counter.ts import { forge } from "runeforge"; export const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { increment: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), decrement: (s) => ({ count: s.count - 1 }), reset: () => ({ count: 0 }), }, }); Use it in a component with useStore: // Counter.tsx import { useStore } from "@runeforge/react"; import { counter } from "./stores/counter"; export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return (

); } Notice three things: No provider. The store is just an import — it's already global. The component subscribes to a selector (s.count), not the whole store. Step 3 · A todo list (and a derived store) For richer state, use a slice for todos and another for the filter. Effects can read and write any store, await whatever they want, and report status into a status field. observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Core concepts › Stores Core concept Stores. A store is the unit of state in Runeforge. It owns a single piece of state, exposes actions to update it, and notifies subscribers when it changes. Stores are framework-agnostic — they have no knowledge of React, Solid, or any UI library. Creating a store Use forge() to create one. The shape of the object you pass is the API of the store. import { forge } from "runeforge"; const session = forge({ state: { user: null as User | null, expiresAt: 0 }, actions: { login: (s, user: User, ttl: number) => ({ user, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl }), logout: () => ({ user: null, expiresAt: 0 }), }, }); The returned store is a plain object with these methods, plus your actions as methods: MEMBER SIGNATURE DESCRIPTION get () => State Returns the current state (a frozen snapshot). set (next: Partial<State>) => void Imperative state update. Prefer actions in most cases. subscribe (listener) => unsubscribe Calls listener on every committed state change. select (selector) => SelectedView Returns a derived view that's its own subscribable store. reset () => void Returns to the initial state. Useful in tests. name string Auto-derived debug name, or passed via the options bag. Reading and subscribing The simplest store is read with get() and observed with subscribe(): const current = session.get(); // { user: null, expiresAt: 0 } const off = session.subscribe((next, prev) => { console.log("changed:", prev, "→", next); }); // later off(); State is immutable. Each commit replaces the previous state with a new frozen object. Don't try to mutate s.user.name = "x" — return a new object instead. Runeforge will warn in dev if it detects an in-place mutation. Composing stores Apps usually have several stores. They compose by importing each other and using derive(): import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { session } from "./session"; import { feed } from "./feed"; export const homepage = derive( [session, feed], (s, f) => ({ greeting: s.user ? `Welcome back, ${s.user.name}` : "Welcome", items: s.user ? f.items : f.items.slice(0, 5), }) ); derive only recomputes when one of its inputs changes — and only emits a notification when its output changes (by structural equality). It's the right tool for "computed views" or "memoized selectors". Slicing a store For very large stores, store.select() returns a slice that behaves like its own store: const currentUser = session.select((s) => s.user); currentUser.subscribe((u) => render(u)); // fires only when `s.user` changes — not on `expiresAt` changes Server-side rendering & serialization Every store can be serialized with store.toJSON() and rehydrated with store.fromJSON(). The intended flow on the server is: create stores, prime them with fetched data, render once, ship the dehydrated state along with the HTML. // server session.login(user, 3600_000); const html = renderToString(<App />); const state = { session: session.toJSON(), feed: feed.toJSON() }; // client session.fromJSON(state.session); feed.fromJSON(state.feed); hydrate(<App />); Testing stores Stores are easy to unit-test because they have no framework. Just call actions and assert against store.get(): import { session } from "./session"; beforeEach(() => session.reset()); test("login sets the user and expiry", () => { session.login({ id: 1, name: "Milena" }, 60_000); const s = session.get(); expect(s.user?.name).toBe("Milena"); expect(s.expiresAt).toBeGreaterThan(Date.now()); }); PREVIOUS ← Quickstart NEXT Actions & selectors → ON THIS PAGE Stores Creating a store Reading and subscribing Composing stores Slicing a store SSR & ser

observation.title: Actions & selectors — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Docs › Core concepts › Actions & selectors Core concept Actions & selectors. Actions describe how state changes. Selectors describe how state is read. Together they give you a one-way data flow without the ceremony of Redux. Actions An action is a function on a store. It receives the current state and any arguments you pass, and returns the next state — or a partial of it. const cart = forge({ state: { items: [] as Item[], coupon: null as string | null }, actions: { add: (s, item: Item) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) }), apply: (s, code: string) => ({ coupon: code }), clear: () => ({ items: [], coupon: null }), }, }); // call them like methods cart.add({ id: 1, name: "Espresso", price: 3.50 }); cart.apply("BLOOM10"); Rules of thumb Return, don't mutate. Always return a new object. Spread, map, filter — but never assign in place. Return a partial. The partial is shallow-merged with current state, so you only return what changed. Stay synchronous if possible. Keep async work in effects (see the Async & effects guide). It makes actions trivially testable. Name actions for what they do, not how they do it. checkout() is better than setCheckoutState(true). Selectors A selector is a pure function from state to a derived value. Components — and any subscriber, really — use selectors so they only re-render when the value they care about changes. const totalPrice = (s: ReturnType<typeof cart.get>) => s.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0); cart.subscribe((s) => render(totalPrice(s))); // fires every change cart.select(totalPrice).subscribe(render); // fires only when total actually changes Composing selectors Selectors compose like any other pure functions. For more involved derivations across multiple stores, prefer derive() — it caches and only recomputes when its inputs change. import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { cart, coupons } from "./stores"; export const grandTotal = derive([cart, coupons], (c, cs) => { const sub = c.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price, 0); const off = c.coupon ? cs.discountFor(c.coupon) : 0; return { sub, discount: off, total: Math.max(0, sub - off) }; }); Reusable action creators For common patterns, Runeforge ships builder helpers like asyncSlice(), listSlice(), and formSlice(). They generate action sets so you don't write the same CRUD by hand. import { forge, listSlice } from "runeforge"; type Todo = { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }; export const todos = forge({ state: listSlice<Todo>().state, actions: listSlice<Todo>().actions("id"), }); // generated: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count todos.add({ id: 1, text: "Write docs", done: false }); todos.update(1, (t) => ({ done: true })); Action middleware Middleware wraps actions. Use it for logging, time-travel, persistence, and analytics. Middleware are pure functions that run before and after every commit. import { use } from "runeforge"; use((next) => (action, args) => { const t0 = performance.now(); const r = next(action, args); console.log(`${action.store}.${action.name}`, `${(performance.now() - t0).toFixed(1)}ms`); return r; }); The order is the order you call use() in. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. observation.title: Examples — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) ☾ ★ 18.4k Docs › Examples Examples Apps you can fork. Self-contained example apps. Every one of them is under 500 lines and uses just the public API. Clone the repo, npm i, npm dev — that's the whole setup. All (12) Beginner Intermediate Advanced SSR beginner Counter (the canonical hello-world) The smallest possible Runeforge app. Single store, three actions, one component. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. Three things to remember Why another state library? Next steps Edit this page on GitHub → Discuss on the forum

Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) bun add runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) bun add runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; import { useStore } from "@runeforge/solid"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }) }, }); export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return <button onClick={counter.inc}>{count()}</button>; } Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) bun add runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy <!-- Counter.vue --> <script setup> import { forge } from "runeforge"; import { useStore } from "@runeforge/vue"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }) }, }); const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); </script> <template> <button @click="counter.inc">{{ count }}</button> </template> Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: Examples — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) ☾ ★ 18.4k Docs › Examples Examples Apps you can fork. Self-contained example apps. Every one of them is under 500 lines and uses just the public API. Clone the repo, npm i, npm dev — that's the whole setup. All (12) Beginner Intermediate Advanced SSR beginner Counter (the canonical hello-world) The smallest possible Runeforge app. Single store, three actions, one component. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart →

Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react) HOOK useStore(store, selector?,

A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react) HOOK useStore(store, selector?,

observation.title: Examples — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) ☾ ★ 18.4k Docs › Examples Examples Apps you can fork. Self-contained example apps. Every one of them is under 500 lines and uses just the public API. Clone the repo, npm i, npm dev — that's the whole setup. All (12) Beginner Intermediate Advanced SSR beginner Counter (the canonical hello-world) The smallest possible Runeforge app. Single store, three actions, one component. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC
